commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Never allocate GPU pages without host backing
commits.pr_body:
## Description

When the HiSparse host pool fills, `HiSparseSourceManager.allocate_new_blocks` gives new pages a null host entry. Those pages are never written back, so they never become clean and their GPU blocks can never be reclaimed: they stay pinned for the life of the request. Freeing host capacity does not fix it, because later allocations extend the host table and the freed blocks go to new tail pages, never to the old null ones. Host prefix publication for the request also stalls at the first null page.

The result is GPU KV pressure and preemptions that HiSparse is meant to prevent, plus lost host prefix-cache coverage, persisting after host capacity has recovered.

Fix: never allocate a page without host backing (alternative to #58963, which backfills null pages after the fact):

- `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` requires host blocks for every page being allocated, not just external-load destinations, and reuses the existing admission sentinel when they don't fit. The scheduler then waits or preempts exactly as it does for GPU exhaustion.
- The best-effort `allocate_new_blocks` override (null padding) is deleted.
- `has_pending_reclamation` also reports host blocks that an in-flight write-back will return (freed request, spill not yet acked), so the scheduler waits a step instead of over-preempting.
- Startup rejects a host pool that cannot hold one `max_model_len` request (plus the null block and a copy-on-write tail), which would otherwise livelock.

## Effect on KV-cache memory over time

**Before.** While the host pool is full, every page a running request seals gets a null host entry and keeps its GPU block for the rest of the request. The pinned set only grows: host blocks freed later go to new tail pages, never to the old null ones. A request that decodes through a host-full window therefore holds GPU KV proportional to the tokens produced during that window, as if HiSparse were off for those pages, and releases it only when it finishes or is preempted. Across the batch, GPU free blocks drift down while the host stays full, and the scheduler preempts (and later recomputes) requests that HiSparse should have kept running. Prefix publication for those requests also stops at the first null page, so the host prefix cache never covers the rest of their context.

**After.** Every GPU-resident page has a host page, so its GPU footprint is transient: a sealed page is dirty until its write-back completes (about one step), stays pinned while within the two-page active tail, and is unpinned once the request can read from host (it has a hot region). Unpinned pages stay readable but count as free, so the GPU pool reclaims them under pressure. Per-request GPU usage is bounded by the hot region, the active tail and in-flight write-backs, independent of context length, for as long as the request runs.

The host pool becomes the hard capacity limit instead: running requests together hold one host block per computed page, and when it is full, new allocations wait or preempt even if GPU blocks are free. Since HiSparse only pays off when the host pool is much larger than the GPU pool, this replaces the gradual, hard-to-see GPU buildup above with a rare, explicit admission limit.

## Related

- #58963 fixes the same bug by backfilling host blocks for null pages after capacity frees up (one page per step). This PR prevents the null pages instead, which removes rather than adds state; only one of the two should land.
- #57457 also edits `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` (counts GPU copies pinned by a host-prefix hit). The changes compose: its copy-pin count replaces this PR's final `return 0`.
- #58949's steady-state concurrency estimate assumes resident pages spill to host; this PR makes that hold under host pressure, and its host-pool gauges become the direct signal for the new admission limit.

## Test Plan

Repro on main (unit-level): with a 3-block host pool, the request's pages 1-3 get null host entries; after the donor frees its block, the capacity goes to new tail page 4, and pages 1-3 stay pinned (`ref_cnt=1`) indefinitely while page 5 is null again.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -q
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -v
```

## Test Result

- CPU: 341 passed; other HiSparse-tagged suites (scheduler, NIXL HMA, stats, config): 22 passed.
- e2e (B300, reduced DeepSeek-V3.2, dummy weights): 3 passed. The new `test_hisparse_host_exhaustion_defers_requests` fails on main (a scheduled request has a null host page).

Accuracy with trained weights and serving throughput under host pressure were not measured.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU][DiffusionGemma] Support narrower canvas w/ sync scheduling
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes DiffusionGemma structured reads on the CPU backend.

Structured reads were added to DiffusionGemma in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57250 and tested on GPU. On CPU they fail with the faster narrower canvases. When async scheduling is disabled, reads that ask for a canvas narrower than the served one are rejected. CPU always runs synchronous scheduling (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31525), and the error asks for `--async-scheduling`, but CPU ignores that flag.

The same happens on any platform started with `--no-async-scheduling`.

This PR adds a synchronous diffusion scheduler that trims each request's canvas to its own width. The async diffusion scheduler already does this. Other models are not affected.

### Changes in this PR

- Add a `DiffusionScheduler` for sync scheduling. It cuts each request's canvas down to the width the request asked for, in `update_draft_token_ids()`. `DiffusionAsyncScheduler` now inherits from it.
- `VllmConfig` selects the matching diffusion scheduler for both sync and async scheduling.
- Remove the check that rejected narrow canvases unless `--async-scheduling` was set.
- Update the structured diffusion README and the tests in `tests/test_sampling_params.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` to match.

No open issue or PR covers this. I searched for `diffusion_canvas_length`, DiffusionGemma on CPU and CPU async scheduling for diffusion. The closest is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58964, which fixed a separate DiffusionGemma crash on CPU. Structured reads still fail on CPU after that fix. 

I used Codex to help with this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C, Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at 32cc3f1ea8, with the real `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` checkpoint in BF16.

**Unit tests:**

```bash
pytest -v tests/test_sampling_params.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
```

**End to end:**

1. Before and after. Send a read with a 32-token canvas to a server with a 64-token canvas, on `main` and with this PR.
2. Correctness. Compare that read with a full-width read on a server with a 32-token canvas. Both give the model the same 32 tokens. The logprobs of 8 label ids at the answer position should match.
3. Serving. Run `vllm serve` with `structured_server.py` in front of it, as in the example README. Send the README's `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/systemone` requests with an outage ticket and a typo ticket. Then send a plain chat completion straight to vLLM.

```bash
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=8 vllm serve google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it --served-model-name dgemma \
    --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 64}' --max-logprobs 32 --enable-prefix-caching \
    --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 8
python examples/features/structured_diffusion/structured_server.py --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --tokenizer google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it --canvas 64 --port 8011
```

## Test Result

Before (`main`), the read fails. The issue has the full traceback and the `collect_env.py` output.

```text

```

After:

- Unit tests: 276 passed.
- The narrow read now works. `DiffusionScheduler` serves it, and its logprobs at the answer position match the full-width read exactly (max difference 0 across 8 label ids). Both answer "yes" with p = 0.89.
- Through `structured_server.py`, `/v1/systemone` gives 0.91 urgency for the outage ticket (4 reads, 2.0 s) and 0.00006 for the typo ticket (1 read, 0.7 s). Every request returns HTTP 200, and the server logs show no errors.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend][RL] Add a weight checker dev endpoint
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Verify that an RL weight update (`start_weight_update → update_weights* → finish_weight_update`) reached every engine and every parameter intact, so a silent partial update does not turn into off-policy training. RFC: #52689

## Design

One dev endpoint, `POST /weight_checker` (requires `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`), in both the Python and Rust frontends:

| Request | Response |
| --- | --- |
| `{"action": "checksum"}` | `{"checksums": {key: sha256_hex}}` |
| `{"action": "reset"}` | `{"status": "reset"}` |
| `{"action": "compare", "baseline": {key: sha256_hex}}` | `{"match": bool, "mismatches": [key]}` |

- Keys are `dp{dp}:pp{pp}:pcp{pcp}:tp{tp}:{param_name}` (the EP rank is determined by dp, pcp and tp). The DP part uses `data_parallel_index`, because dense workers reset `data_parallel_rank` to 0. Duplicate keys across workers return 500 instead of silently merging ranks.
- Coverage is the model's parameters, which is what weight loading writes. Buffers are excluded because loading never restores them; zeroing them (e.g. FP8 KV scales) would make `compare` fail forever. `SharedWeightParameter` partitions and tensor-subclass weights (e.g. TorchAO `qdata`/`scale`) are expanded into their inner tensors.
- `reset` zeroes the covered tensors in place through `collective_rpc`, the same path as `update_weights`.
- `checksum` and `compare` use a new `EngineClient.compute_weight_checksums`. The async client calls a `compute_weight_checksums` engine utility on every managed engine through `call_utility_all_async` (#59240) and concatenates the results. `collective_rpc` is unchanged: under DP load balancing it returns only the first engine's result, and each engine holds different shards. The Rust frontend's `collective_rpc` already gathers every engine, so its route calls it directly.
- The endpoint is stateless and the caller holds the baseline. With several API processes, `checksum` and `compare` can land on different processes.
- `action` and `baseline` are embedded body fields, like the neighboring endpoints. An unknown action or `compare` without `baseline` returns 400.

Documented limitations (`docs/training/weight_checker.md`): stay paused from `checksum` to `compare` (EPLB moves experts while serving); send to every API server under external LB; draft models, LoRA adapters and buffers are not checked; CPU backends that repack linear weights, compressed-tensors online transforms, `--offload-backend prefetch`, and MoE padding beyond the checkpoint shape (DeepEP, MXFP4) are not supported; the engine must be awake.

Depends on #57163: until it lands, compressed-tensors checkpoints expose the attention KV scales as parameters, so `reset` zeroes them and nothing restores them.

## Not a duplicate

This is the existing PR for RFC #52689. No other open PR adds a weight-checksum endpoint.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_checksum.py
pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/state_transitions/test_weight_checker.py
```

- Unit (CPU): every parameter is covered; reset changes every parameter and no buffer; strided and 0-dim parameters; `SharedWeightParameter` partitions; tensor-subclass inner tensors; distinct dense-DP key prefixes; the DPLB client gathers checksums from every engine (`tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py`).
- Rust: route merges worker checksums, compares, resets, and rejects invalid requests before any engine call (`rust/src/server/src/routes/tests.rs`).
- E2E (Qwen3-0.6B): 400 on invalid requests; stable checksums; `compare` reports changed and missing keys; reset → `reload_weights` → match; reset → real IPC weight transfer over HTTP → match; DP=2 and TP=2 (2 GPUs): every worker rank is reported, reset, and restored.
- CI: the unit tests and single-GPU e2e tests run in existing jobs. The 2-GPU e2e tests (DP=2, TP=2) need 2 GPUs, and the CPU unit test covers the engine fan-out in CI.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 6 passed.
- E2E: 10 passed (single GPU, IPC transfer, DP=2, TP=2) on GB200 in a nightly container with the PR applied.
- Rust route tests: 2 passed (`cargo test -p vllm-server weight_checker`); rustfmt and clippy clean.
- Parallel topologies on the current head, same container: TP2, PP2, DP2, TP2+EP, DP2+EP (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and TP2xPP2 all pass: every worker rank covered, stable checksums, reload-only match, reset → reload match with token-identical greedy output (4 prompts × 32 tokens), and single-rank and 1-ULP corruption reported as exactly one key. FP8 compressed-tensors fails reset → reload until #57163.
- TorchAO `Float8WeightOnlyConfig` checksum/reset verified manually with torchao 0.18.
- pre-commit (ruff, mypy, markdownlint) clean.
- No model output path changes, so no accuracy eval.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change. The implementation went through ten rounds of adversarial review with Codex and Kimi K3 until both reported no findings. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Resolve MTP verification rows with a union residency kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Resolve all of a request's MTP verification rows with one union residency kernel, on every sparse MLA backend, and drop the fragile routing that worked around the old kernel.

The old `hisparse_resolve_residency_kernel` ran one block per row, but `device_global_indices` and the LRU are per request, so two rows of one request in one launch could claim the same free slot and read each other's KV. Callers avoided that by resolving verification one step per launch (FlashMLA, FlashInfer TRTLLM) or by treating it as prefill (backends without `hisparse_supports_multi_token_decode`). On FlashAttn sparse MLA a FULL CUDA graph froze that prefill path's residency check at capture, so replays with spilled pages still hit the race. Found via #59036's CI failure (`test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore`).

## Changes

- **Union kernel.** Each request's first-row block resolves all its rows: one hash-table union of host misses, one LRU walk, eviction slots in deterministic (row, top-k) order, one LRU rewrite. Each host row is copied once per request; a reused slot counts as a hit. The table is sized from `max_decode_query_len * index_topk` (~90 KB for GLM-5.3 + MTP3, MTP ≤ 9 at `index_topk=2048`), checked at startup; a union past that bound traps.
- **One routing path.** Verification resolves in one `swap_in` per layer, and `hisparse_supports_multi_token_decode` is removed, so every backend keeps verification as decode. Request ids (with CUDA-graph padding rows masked) live in a group-owned buffer, since the resolver reads them on the copy stream.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_speculative_rows_resolve_host_misses_consistently` (disjoint, overlapping, and multi-pass rows) plus unit tests for hit counting, union-bound sizing, the startup check, spec-as-decode, and padding/request-id handling.
- HiSparse kernel, sparse MLA backend, and e2e tests; #59036 applied on top.
- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 + MTP3 on B200 (FlashInfer TRTLLM, HiSparse under spill pressure), and a layer-level benchmark on H100.

## Test Result

- Race test fails 30/30 on main's kernel and passes with this PR; HiSparse tests pass (H100, H200, B200); `test_hisparse.py` passes, also with #59036.
- GLM-5.3 B200: MTP acceptance in line with main (1.06–1.32 vs 1.19 per window on random prompts); a shrunk GLM-5.3 config matches main's tokens and drafts exactly under FULL graphs.

Decode residency per layer, µs (H100, MTP3, `index_topk=2048`, main → this PR). **Bold** = faster by >5%.

| Mode | Regime | 1 req | 8 reqs | 32 reqs | 64 reqs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph | steady | 155 → **64** | 185 → **87** | 264 → **167** | 373 → **268** |
| | cold | 189 → **129** | 582 → **539** | 2119 → 2174 | 4213 → 4139 |

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the root cause was reproduced and validated on H200, H100, and B200.

## Summary

Fix the main-branch pre-commit failure introduced by #59286 ([failed job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/36655375579/job/109699177322)). `OpenAIServingModels.engine_client` is typed as `EngineClient`, so mypy sees `add_lora` as an async method and rejects `assert_not_called()`, even though the test creates it with `MagicMock(spec=EngineClient)`.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Use the MiMo structural-tag builder
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Rust MiMo tool parser reuses the Qwen3-Coder structural-tag builder, whose tags are newline-delimited: `<tool_call>\n<function=NAME>\n`, with trigger `<tool_call>\n<function=`. MiMo's template and model output are compact: `<tool_call><function=NAME><parameter=K>…</parameter></function></tool_call>`.

- `auto` + strict: the model's output never reaches the trigger, so the whole tool call is treated as free text and strict constrains nothing.
- `required` / named: the grammar forces the newline layout, which is off the model's training distribution, so the model is steered off-distribution or the request cannot complete.

This is the Rust counterpart of #58019 (Python side, which depends on mlc-ai/xgrammar#916). The Rust MiMo parser came from #57933.

The fix bumps `xgrammar-structural-tag` to 0.4.1 (synced with XGrammar 0.2.8, which adds the `mimo` builder; released from Inferact/xgrammar-structural-tag; 0.4.1 also makes `normalize_tool_choice` public, for callers that build formats directly such as the stacked Kimi K3 output grammar) and points `MiMoToolParser` at `Model::Mimo`.

- The same sync adds `excludes` to `JsonSchemaFormat`, so every serialized `json_schema` node now carries `"excludes": []`. The `KimiK3` snapshot in `unified/kimi_k3/structural_tag.rs` is updated for that. vLLM's own K3 builder does not populate `excludes` yet; that is out of scope here.
- This PR does not bump the engine's `xgrammar == 0.2.7` pin. The 0.4 output for MiMo, Kimi K3, Qwen3.5 and Llama compiles with XGrammar 0.2.7 (`excludes` is ignored there), and the MiMo tags use only fields 0.2.7 already understands.

Duplicate check: the open-PR search for MiMo structural tags finds only #58019 (Python frontend) and the output-grammar replay harness #59143, which this unblocks and which does not change the builder.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
```

## Test Result

- 1287 tests passed across `vllm-parser`, `vllm-chat` and `vllm-server`. The new `structural_tag_uses_compact_mimo_tags` test asserts the `<tool_call>` trigger and the compact begin/end tags.
- Clippy and fmt pass. The workspace-wide nextest run needs `libpython3.14` for the PyO3 `tool-parser` binary, which is missing on this host, so that binary was not run.
- In `xgrammar-structural-tag` itself: Python parity against XGrammar 0.2.8 for all 18 upstream models, plus matcher checks that MiMo accepts the compact call and rejects the newline form.
- Not covered here: end-to-end `tool_call_mix` replay for MiMo under `required` / named. That lands in the stacked replay harness (#59143).

commits.pr_title: [Core][BugFix] Tag prefix-cache extra keys by source
commits.pr_body:
## What this fixes

Prefix-cache block hashes mix LoRA names, `cache_salt`, multimodal identifiers and
prompt-embeds digests into a single untagged `extra_keys` tuple. For example, a LoRA
request for adapter `foo` and a base-model request with `cache_salt="foo"` produce the
same first-block hash for the same prompt tokens. Either request can then be served KV
computed with the other's weights, and a caller can choose a salt that lands in an
adapter's cache namespace. Fixes #44701.

Each extra-key component is now tagged with its source:

| Source | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| LoRA | `name` | `("lora", name)` |
| `cache_salt` | `salt` | `("cache_salt", salt)` |
| Multimodal | `(identifier, offset)` | `("mm", identifier, offset)` |
| Prompt embeds | `digest` | `("prompt_embeds", digest)` |

Equal values from different fields can no longer produce the same key.

KV cache events keep publishing the previous untagged shapes (see Compatibility), via
`to_event_extra_keys()` where `BlockStored` events are built.

An earlier revision of this PR also changed how an image's EXIF `ImageID` is used by the
multimodal hasher. That part was dropped, so this PR does not change
`vllm/multimodal/hasher.py`.

## Compatibility

- Block hashes change for every block that has LoRA, `cache_salt`, multimodal or
  prompt-embeds extra keys. KV offloaded or persisted by an earlier version under those
  hashes will no longer match; it misses rather than being reused.
- KV cache events are unchanged: `BlockStored.extra_keys` still carries the untagged
  values (bare LoRA name and `cache_salt`, `(identifier, offset)` pairs, bare
  prompt-embeds digests), because external consumers such as KV-aware routers parse
  those shapes and can fail to decode the tagged tuples. Consumers that rebuild block
  keys from events can tell the values apart using `lora_name` and the fixed order
  (LoRA, multimodal, `cache_salt`, prompt embeds). `BlockStored.block_hashes` carries
  the new hashes.

## Related PRs

- Supersedes #44706 (now closed), which tagged only the LoRA and `cache_salt` keys.
- Uses the same `("lora", ...)` tagging style as #48352 (LoRA identity keys for
  same-name reloads), so the two combine cleanly.

Advisory: GHSA-rh6f-3x46-j33q

Track B: this is a public PR against `vllm-project/vllm@main`.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache tests/v1/simple_kv_offload \
  tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
```

- `test_lora_name_and_cache_salt_block_hashes_do_not_collide` checks that the first
  block hashes differ. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- Existing assertions on hash inputs were updated to the tagged form, including tests
  added on main since this PR was opened.
- The existing KV event tests
  (`test_cache_partial_block_event_keeps_every_mm_feature`,
  `test_eager_store_lora_metadata`) are unchanged from main and still pass, so the
  event format is unchanged. Without the event conversion both fail.
- On 4x GB200: the command above gives 977 passed, 8 skipped, and 2 errors in
  `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate` that also occur on main.
- A wider run (`tests/v1/core`, `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit`, `tests/v1/kv_offload`,
  `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload`, `tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py`) failed
  exactly the same set of tests with and without this PR (gated models and
  environment-dependent engine startup), apart from one test whose fix is included here.

## Maintainer update

@njhill rebased this onto current main, moved the new test into
`tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, and updated the tests that asserted untagged key
shapes. The authors' source change is unchanged. A follow-up commit keeps the KV event
format unchanged. AI assistance (Claude) was used for the rebase, the test updates,
the event-format commit and the test runs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Responses API] Build streamed final response from streamed items
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

In non-harmony streaming, `/v1/responses` builds `response.completed` by re-parsing the full output instead of reusing what it streamed, and the two disagree. Items get new ids and a function call's `call_id` changes, so a client that continues with `previous_response_id` references a `call_id` the stored response doesn't have. Streamed items can also go missing (e.g. a whitespace-only message before a tool call), and logprobs move from the message to every generated token.

This PR builds `response.completed` from the streamed items. Streamed items get `rs_` / `msg_` / `fc_` ids and the parser's `call_id`, as in non-streaming, and the done message carries its text logprobs. `function_call_arguments.done` is now always emitted, including for calls with no argument deltas, as the Harmony path does.

Related: #47916 fixes only function-call ids, #54064 bundles a similar change with unrelated work, and #54236 overlaps on `function_call_arguments.done`.

## Test Plan

Live A/B on one H200: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, base `1d331f8341` vs. this PR, both servers started with:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --max-logprobs 5
```

Four streaming `/v1/responses` requests at temperature 0: a single tool call, two parallel tool calls, a zero-argument tool, and plain text with output logprobs. For each, every `response.output_item.done` item is compared with `response.completed.response.output` (id, `call_id`, arguments, text, logprob count), each function call is checked for a `function_call_arguments.done`, and the same request is sent non-streaming to compare usage.

```bash
curl -sN localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "input": "What'"'"'s the weather in Paris?", "stream": true, "temperature": 0,
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get current weather for a city",
             "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}]
}' | grep -E '"type":"response.(output_item.done|completed)"'
```

## Test Result

| Request | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Single tool call | streamed `reasoning`, `message "\n\n"`, `function_call` (`call_id` `call_86cf…`); completed `reasoning`, `function_call` (`call_id` `chatcmpl-tool-937d…`); all ids differ | streamed == completed: `rs_b195…`, `msg_b916…`, `fc_a37a…` with `call_id` `chatcmpl-tool-8f95…` |
| Two parallel tool calls | completed drops the message; both calls get new ids and `call_id`s | streamed == completed |
| Zero-argument tool | completed drops the message; ids and `call_id` differ | streamed == completed |
| Text with logprobs | streamed message 0 logprobs, completed 103 (all tokens) | 3 and 3 (`"\n\n"`, `Hello`, `!`) |
| Usage, stream vs non-stream | output 104 / 125 / 110 / 103, reasoning 81 / 81 / 91 / 97 | identical |

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][Perf] Add TP=2/4/8 per-rank shapes to the sm_120 batch-invariant matmul table
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #57456. The `sm120` family of `_BATCH_INVARIANT_MATMUL_TUNED_CONFIGS` only covered the TP=1 shapes of Qwen3-1.7B / 4B / 8B, so with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and `tensor_parallel_size > 1` every linear layer on RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50 still ran the batch-invariant persistent matmul with the default `128x128x64 / 8 warps / 3 stages` config (the TP=2 rows in #57456's comments show the resulting ~2.9x BI overhead unchanged by the table). Now that #57586 selects the tile config from the runtime M, the table is the remaining lever for TP.

This PR adds the 41 per-rank `(N, K)` shapes of the same three models at TP=2 / 4 / 8 (`qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` and the vocab-parallel `lm_head`; `(3072, 4096)` is shared by Qwen3-8B TP=2 qkv_proj and TP=8 gate_up_proj), 15 -> 56 entries. Same structure and invariance rule as the existing entries: one `BLOCK_K` per `(N, K)`, `BLOCK_M / BLOCK_N / num_warps / num_stages` per M bucket.

## Method

Identical to #57456 (same sweep tool, same gates), one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 188 SMs, driver 580.159.04), vLLM main @ 9ef37771b, torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1: per shape 3 `BLOCK_K` x 4 `BLOCK_M` x 4 `BLOCK_N` x 2 warps x 4 stages = 384 configs x 10 M values (1 ... 2048), CUDA-event timed against the current default config and cuBLAS; `BLOCK_K` chosen shape-wide by a decode-weighted score; gate: `allclose` to an fp32 reference and the M = 1 rows **bitwise identical** to the same rows computed at M = 8 / 32 / 256 / 2048 (sha256). All 41 shapes green.

## Kernel-level results (p50, tuned vs current default; geomean over M buckets)

Geomean per model: Qwen3-1.7B: decode 1.70x, all M 1.43x (max 8.21x, min 0.85x) / Qwen3-4B: decode 2.06x, all M 1.61x (max 8.86x, min 0.81x) / Qwen3-8B: decode 2.38x, all M 1.78x (max 9.36x, min 0.98x).

| model | TP | shape | N | K | BLOCK_K | decode (M<=64) | all M | max | min (M) |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reject a prefix_match_unit that a single KV cache group cannot honor
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58020.

With a single KV cache group, `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` uses the block size as the hash unit and drops `--prefix-match-unit` without a warning. The Mamba prefill checkpoint builder (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/checkpoint.py`, used by the Kimi-K3 KDA path with FlashKDA) still reads the flag. It writes the checkpoint for a different position than the one the scheduler registers for that block, and a later prefix-cache hit resumes from the wrong recurrent state. Nothing errors.

This rejects a `prefix_match_unit` other than the block size when there is exactly one group and block hashing is active (prefix caching or a KV connector), the same condition the multi-group path checks before it reads the flag. The flag's docstring already requires every group's block size to be divisible by it, and one group can't honor anything else.

#58020 proposed propagating the resolved unit to the workers. The case above is the only divergence I could reach. With the flag unset, align mode sets the Mamba block size to the attention block size (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`), so the builder's fallback equals the resolver's GCD. #56960 moves the same builder into the shared GDN metadata path, and this check covers it there too.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/kv_connector/unit
```

The suites were also run on clean `main` in a separate worktree with the same packages. On an H100 NVL: the repro below on `main` and this branch, plus `lm_eval` gsm8k and `vllm bench serve` with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`.

## Test Result

- The resolver called directly: it raises for one group with prefix caching or a connector on and a different flag, and returns the block size with the flag unset or equal, with prefix caching and connectors off, and with no KV cache groups.
- `tests/v1/core` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` on CPU: every failure also fails on `main` (`e440b75`) from the environment (no CUDA, no ray, gated models), apart from Hugging Face 429s. Those were rerun three times on both trees and passed each time.
- `test_mooncake_store_worker.py` builds `cache_config` as a `SimpleNamespace`, so the stub gains `prefix_match_unit=None`.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files: passed.

The GPU runs below were on `3300c8c`, before the check was gated on block hashing. The repro enables prefix caching, so it takes the same path.

Repro, a tiny all-KDA `KimiLinearForCausalLM` with seeded random weights and a 2040-token prompt:

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 python repro_kda_checkpoint.py \
    --layout kda-only --prefix-match-unit 32 --block-size 16 --splice 2016:2032
```

On `main` the worker writes the checkpoint at 2016 into the slot the scheduler registers as 2032. The cached request matches a cold run of the prompt with tokens 2016-2031 removed exactly (max first-step top-20 logprob diff 0.0) and differs from the plain cold run by 0.0464. On this branch the command stops at startup:

```text
ValueError: Invalid prefix_match_unit=32; with a single KV cache group, prefix-cache hits land on the block size (16). Unset it or set it to 16.
```

Without the flag, and with one MLA layer added (two groups, flag honored), both arms produce byte-identical output.

`lm_eval` gsm8k 5-shot through `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --language-model-only`: flexible-extract 0.3601 on `main`, 0.3571 here (stderr 0.0132).

`vllm bench serve`, random dataset with a 512-token shared prefix plus 512 input tokens, 128 output, 400 prompts, concurrency 64, seeds 0-2, three rounds per arm with the last two interleaved: output throughput 6598 tok/s on `main` and 6422 here, sd about 400 on both, and the per-round gap changes sign. The shared prefix is shorter than the 544-token block, so there were no prefix-cache hits, and the model has four KV cache groups, so the new check is not on this path. Treat it as a regression check.

Full logs, sha256sums and scripts are attached in the review thread.

## Not a duplicate

```bash
gh issue view 58020 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "58020 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "prefix_match_unit"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes"
```

No open PR validates `prefix_match_unit` for single-group models. #56960 touches the checkpoint builder but not the resolver.

AI assistance was used for parts of this change. I have reviewed every changed line and can defend the design end to end.

## Purpose

Responses built-in tool execution currently creates a new random
`function_call_output.call_id` instead of preserving the ID of the function
call that triggered it. The resulting tool-role message can no longer be
correlated with the assistant tool call in the next model turn.

This affects the MCP client-session paths for code interpreter, web search,
and container execution, as well as the local demo-server code interpreter.

Fixes #55592.

- Correct the `ParsableContext` helper annotations to match the runtime
  `ResponseFunctionToolCall` objects.
- Add regression coverage through the public `ParsableContext.call_tool()`
  dispatch path for MCP and local tools.

## Prior and adjacent work

PR #47537 proposed the same protocol invariant but was closed without merging
and did not cover the local `HarmonyPythonTool` path.

PR #47916 is distinct: it aligns streamed function-call events with the final
completed response and does not change built-in tool outputs.

PR #55540 fixes malformed JSON retry behavior. It overlaps only in the
`ParsableContext` type annotations and the existing unit-test file; the
runtime fixes are independent. I will rebase this PR after either change

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] GLM-5.3-Flash: fp8 plan dtype on SM90 sparse MLA, and right-size the indexer prefill workspace
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

## Not a duplicate

- #51252 divides the *builder's* chunk budget by `compress_ratio` for DeepSeek; this is
  the model-side `max_total_seq_len` for GLM-5.3. Per @nood-co1 the two compose.
- #54743 scopes offload group configs to prefix-cacheable groups; different file,
  different failure.
- Searched open PRs for `get_max_prefill_buffer_size`, `max_total_seq_len` and the SM90
  sparse backend; nothing else touches these call sites.

## Testing

No unit test covers either path (both need a GLM-5.3 checkpoint and FlashInfer on
Hopper), so this was validated by serving. 2x H200 NVL, TP2, LibertAI NVFP4 weights,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, MTP k=3, CUDA graphs on, CPU offload
with a 256 GiB region. Both fixes have been running in production here since 2026-08-29
and 2026-09-01 respectively.

- fp8 fix: without it the server does not start; with it `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` is
  selected and the KV pool holds 4,503,445 tokens against 2,532,577 in bf16.
- workspace fix: available KV memory 29.44 -> 32.06 GiB, GPU KV cache size
  4,503,445 -> 4,904,494 tokens (+8.9%). Note that run also raised `--max-num-seqs`
  16 -> 32, so part of the freed memory went back into per-sequence buffers.
- Regression battery after the workspace change: needle retrieval on 1M-token prompts
  4/4 at depths 0.05/0.35/0.65/0.95; 32 concurrent 118k-token prompts, 32/32 with 0
  failures and 0 preemptions; an eviction cycle of eleven 500k-token prompts against a
  4.9M-token KV pool, where the return visit is served from CPU offload (61.0s cold,
  3.5s on return, `external_prefix_cache_hits_total` +492,800).

## Model evaluation

fp8 KV against bf16 on the same checkpoint: GSM8K 0.888 vs 0.880, MATH exact 0.9050 vs
0.9071 (symbolic 0.9671 vs 0.9664), MBPP 0.910 vs 0.920, IFEval prompt strict 0.880 /
instruction strict 0.925. All within noise. The workspace change moves no math: same
kernels, same inputs, only a smaller scratch allocation, and the needle battery above is
identical before and after.

AI assistance was used for this work.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor parallel_tool_calls=false in the Responses API
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`/v1/responses` ignores `parallel_tool_calls: false` whenever the grammar doesn't already limit the model to one call. That happens with parsers that have no structural tag, with `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0`, and with `tool_choice: auto`. Chat completions already filters these calls after parsing (`maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`, #44955); Responses never did.

This PR reuses that helper in the non-harmony Responses path, streaming and non-streaming. Only a literal `False` filters, and `None`/`True` behave as before. When streaming, dropped calls emit no events, so `output_index` values stay contiguous.

## Test Plan

Live A/B on one H200: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, base `a96ee5935d` vs. this PR.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes
```

commits.pr_title: [Core] Combine per-engine utility results like the Rust client
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With DP load balancing, `DPLBAsyncMPClient.call_utility_async` sends a utility to every engine but returns only engine 0's result. So in the Python frontend:

- `reset_prefix_cache` reports success even if another engine failed to reset.
- `is_sleeping`, `is_scheduler_paused` and `get_weight_version` report engine 0's state even if other engines disagree.

The Rust client already combines every engine's result for these calls. This PR makes the Python client do the same.

## Changes

`AsyncMPClient` gets the Python counterparts of the Rust client's helpers:

| Python | Rust |
| --- | --- |
| `call_utility_all_async` returns one result per managed engine | `call_utility` |
| `call_utility_consensus_async` returns the shared result and raises if engines differ | `call_utility_consensus` |

These methods now combine per-engine results the same way the Rust client does:

| Method | Combined as |
| --- | --- |
| `reset_prefix_cache` | `all(...)` |
| `is_sleeping`, `is_scheduler_paused`, `get_weight_version` | consensus |

`DPLBAsyncMPClient.call_utility_async` reuses `call_utility_all_async` and still returns engine 0's result.

Unchanged:

- LoRA utilities (`add_lora`, `remove_lora`, `pin_lora`, `list_loras`). Adapters are loaded and evicted per engine on demand, so their results describe engine-local state, and neither `all()` nor consensus is right.
- `get_supported_tasks`.
- `collective_rpc`, a public API whose results callers may read.

**Behavior change (DP load balancing only):** `reset_prefix_cache` returns False if any engine fails. The three consensus methods raise instead of silently returning engine 0's value when engines disagree. Clients with a single engine per frontend behave exactly as before.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR changes how DP utility results are combined. #52864 adds an identical `call_utility_all_async` and uses it for `wake_up`; whichever PR lands second drops its copy on rebase.

## Test Result

- pre-commit (ruff, mypy) clean.
- No dedicated test is included. The combining logic was checked locally with a unit test that mocks two engines (all succeed, one fails, agree, disagree), and all cases passed.
- No model output path changes, so no accuracy eval.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Enforce parallel_tool_calls=false in the required-tool grammar
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `tool_choice="required"`, the structured-output schema built in
`_get_json_schema_from_tools` (`vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py`) is an array with `minItems: 1` and **no
upper bound**, and `parallel_tool_calls` is never consulted — `adjust_request`
(`vllm/tool_parsers/abstract_tool_parser.py`) only passes `tool_choice` and `tools`.

So a client that explicitly sends `parallel_tool_calls: false` still gets a grammar that permits an
unbounded run of tool calls. vLLM lets the model generate them and then discards all but the first
*after the fact*, in `maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`
(`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/tool_calls_utils.py`). Consequences:

- Token budget and latency are spent on calls that are thrown away.
- If the model keeps going until `max_tokens`, `finish_reason` is `"length"` rather than
  `"tool_calls"`.
- Worst case, the budget runs out while the **first** call's arguments are still being emitted, so
  the one tool call the client actually receives is truncated into invalid JSON.

The client asked for at most one tool call; the decoding constraint should enforce that instead of
post-filtering.

### Fix

Thread `parallel_tool_calls` into `get_json_schema_from_tools` and set `"maxItems": 1` when it is
explicitly `False`, so the grammar itself stops after one tool call.

Only a literal `false` opts out — `None` means the field was never set and the default (true)
applies. This matches the convention already used by `maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`
(`if request.parallel_tool_calls is not False`), which was established deliberately in #44955
("Fix parallel_tool_calls: null treated as false instead of default true").

`maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls` is left in place as a safety net for parsers that bypass the
generic grammar (e.g. those setting `supports_required_and_named`, cf. #50180).

Forced named tool choice is unaffected: those branches return a bare parameters object, never an
array.

### Backend compatibility

`maxItems` is supported by the structured-output backends.
`has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py`) rejects
only `uniqueItems`, `contains`, `minContains` and `maxContains` for arrays; `minItems` is already
relied on today by this same schema. `outlines_core` and llguidance both handle `maxItems`.

### Relationship to #50399

This is **related to** #50399, not a fix for it. That reporter used the default `parallel_tool_calls`
(true), where multiple tool calls are legal per the OpenAI spec and the observed looping is
model/template behaviour on GLM-5.2. This change does make `parallel_tool_calls: false` an effective
constraint-level mitigation for that class of runaway generation, and it closes a genuine
spec-compliance gap on its own merits.

### Not a duplicate

Checked before opening: no open PR touches `parallel_tool_calls` in the schema path, and no open PR
references #50399.

```console
$ curl -s "https://api.github.com/search/issues?q=repo:vllm-project/vllm+is:pr+is:open+parallel_tool_calls+maxItems"
total_count: 0
$ curl -s "https://api.github.com/search/issues?q=repo:vllm-project/vllm+is:pr+50399"
total_count: 0
```

## Test Plan

Extended the existing `tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py` (already
`pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test`), reusing its `_compile_and_check` helper, which compiles the
generated schema to a regex via `outlines_core.json_schema.build_regex_from_schema` — the same path
used by the JSON logits processor. No new test file, no model or GPU required.

New `TestParallelToolCallsConstraint` covers:

- `parallel_tool_calls=False` → the compiled grammar matches a one-element array and **rejects** a
  two-element array.
- `parallel_tool_calls=True` / `None` → a two-element array still matches (guards against
  regressing default parallel tool calling).
- The `maxItems` bound is `1` / absent / absent for `False` / `True` / `None`, with `minItems` still
  `1` in all three.
- Forced named tool choice with `parallel_tool_calls=False` still yields a schema with no
  `maxItems`.

```bash
pytest -v tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py
pytest -v tests/tool_parsers/ tests/tool_use/test_gemma4_responses_adjust_request.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py \
    vllm/tool_parsers/abstract_tool_parser.py \
    tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py
```

## Test Result

```console
$ pytest -q tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py
170 passed, 17 warnings in 27.98s
# 163 before this change + 7 new

$ pytest -q tests/tool_parsers/ tests/tool_use/test_gemma4_responses_adjust_request.py \
      tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py \
      --ignore=tests/tool_parsers/test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py
1085 passed, 3 skipped, 34 xfailed, 21 warnings in 591.22s (0:09:51)

$ pre-commit run --files vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py \
      vllm/tool_parsers/abstract_tool_parser.py \
      tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py
ruff check.......................................................Passed
ruff format......................................................Passed
typos............................................................Passed
Run mypy for Python 3.10.........................................Passed
Check SPDX headers...............................................Passed
Check for forbidden imports......................................Passed
```

`tests/tool_parsers/test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py` is excluded above because its fixtures download
a gated Llama tokenizer and error with HF `401 Unauthorized` in this environment. Verified
pre-existing: the same 15 setup errors occur on a clean checkout of `main` without this change.

### Negative control

To confirm the new tests actually catch the bug rather than passing vacuously, the `maxItems`
assignment was temporarily disabled and the suite re-run:

```console
$ pytest -q tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py -k ParallelToolCalls
>       assert matches == should_match
E       assert True == False
>       assert schema.get("maxItems") == expected
E       AssertionError: assert None == 1
FAILED ...::TestParallelToolCallsConstraint::test_disabled_rejects_a_second_tool_call
FAILED ...::TestParallelToolCallsConstraint::test_max_items_bound[False-1]
2 failed, 5 passed
```

Without the fix the grammar demonstrably **accepts** a second tool call under
`parallel_tool_calls: false`, which is the bug.

### Model evaluation

No model eval was run. This change alters generated output only when a request explicitly sets
`parallel_tool_calls: false`, and only by removing continuations from the decoding grammar — there is
no change to weights, kernels, sampling, or the default (`parallel_tool_calls` unset/true) path,
which is covered by the regression tests above. The behavioural claim is verified at the grammar
level in the negative control. A served end-to-end check against a tool-calling model would need GPU
hardware I do not have access to; happy to add e2e results if a maintainer considers them necessary.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Keep the prompt-end prefill checkpoint under sparse retention
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Mamba prefix caching in align mode with internal prefill checkpoints and sparse retention (`retention_interval == 0`) drops the **prompt-end** checkpoint for most prompts. As a result, the next request that extends the prompt misses the entire prefix.

`MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` (added in #56794) treats a checkpoint as request-local and evicts it when `num_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens`. That is right for mid-prompt chunks. But the hybrid coordinator caches the final chunk only up to its last full block (`_align_cacheable`), so whenever the prompt length is not a multiple of the Mamba block size, the condition also holds on the final chunk. The prompt's own reusable checkpoint is then evicted.

Only a later request that happens to stop a chunk at the shared-prefix junction re-materializes the state. So the first follow-up after every new prompt misses, and in a multi-turn session, where each turn extends a prompt that was prefilled exactly once, **every turn misses**.

The existing test (`test_internal_checkpoint_publication_respects_retention`) does not catch this: it uses `hash_block_size < mamba_block_size`, where the final chunk is cached at full prompt length.

### Fix

Keep the checkpoint when its position is the prompt's own final checkpoint position (`get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(num_prompt_tokens, ...)`). Mid-prompt checkpoints are still evicted as before.

## Test Plan

- New test `test_prompt_end_checkpoint_survives_sparse_retention_with_coarse_hash`:
  - `hash_block_size == mamba_block_size`, a non-aligned 240-token prompt, two chunks;
  - checks that the prompt-end checkpoint is published and that a request extending the prompt hits 224 tokens;
  - fails on main, passes with this change.
- `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache`, `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`.
- End to end on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA with prefill checkpoints, B300), sending a prefix-only prompt, then 3 requests extending it:

| | TP2: hit on the 1st / 2nd follow-up | TP1 ranks (DEP4): hit on the 1st / 2nd follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0 / 193,280 | 0 / 192,000 |
| this PR | 193,280 / 193,280 | 192,000 / 192,000 |

## Test Result

- Unit tests on this branch: 317 passed across the files above, including the new test.
- `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` could not run in this environment: engine init fails in the Qwen3.5 GDN path with an unrelated `chunk_gated_delta_rule(... backend=...)` TypeError from the local library versions.
- Multi-session P/D serving (GLM-5.3-Flash, DEP4 prefill + DEP4 decode), prefill-side prefix hit rate:
  - main: 87.9%, i.e. one full miss per session;
  - this PR: 96.97%, the block-granularity ceiling.
  - TTFT p90 dropped from 16.7 s to 0.76 s.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KV Connector][Mooncake] Pack hybrid/MLA KV into coalesced transfer regions
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Mooncake PD currently emits one RDMA descriptor per layer-view × block. Hybrid/MLA caches (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) expand into many views of one packed allocation.

Page-contiguous views stay addressable by layer name so heterogeneous PP can align the shared layers (#56033). Views in the same KV group merge across in-page padding. A run that starts at row offset 0 on both sides is lifted to the full row, so consecutive blocks coalesce. Groups are not merged: they overlay one row and own different block ids. A non-contiguous packed row is one region at the allocation. Mismatched PP rejects that shape. Mamba / KpoolTail stay unpacked. HNC-contiguous FA stays one region per layer.

There is **no extra_config flag**. Handshake carries layer names, group ids, and each view's row offset.

Relative to `origin/main`, `mooncake_connector.py` is +474 / −42 (net 432, under the 500-line RFC bar). No docs change: no new user-facing extra_config.

commits.pr_title: [MRV2] Add DRY as a custom logits processor example
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Related to #8581.

This adds DRY ("Don't Repeat Yourself") as an example of a Model Runner V2 custom logits processor, in `examples/features/logits_processor/dry.py` with a runnable demo and a README entry. `tests/v1/sample/test_dry.py` imports from the example. Nothing else changes. No other open PR adds DRY; #57620, an example built on this code, is closed.

DRY is a repetition penalty ported from llama.cpp's `llama_sampler_dry_apply`. It follows p-e-w's scheme for text-generation-webui, via pi6am's koboldcpp port and llama.cpp's. A token that would extend a repeat of at least `dry_allowed_length` tokens loses `multiplier * base ** (repeat_length - allowed_length)` from its logit.

Pass the class with `LLM(..., logits_processors=[DryState])`, or load it with `--logits-processors examples.features.logits_processor.dry:DryState` when the repository root is on the import path. A request turns DRY on by setting `dry_multiplier` in `SamplingParams.extra_args` (`vllm_xargs` over HTTP) and can also set `dry_base`, `dry_allowed_length`, `dry_penalty_last_n` and `dry_sequence_breakers`. Any other `dry_*` key fails the request.

Parameter names, defaults, the float32 rounding of `dry_multiplier` and `dry_base`, the exponent clamp and breaker containment follow llama.cpp at `ec928150`, apart from the differences below.

<details><summary>Differences from llama.cpp</summary>

| | llama.cpp | this example |
|---|---|---|
| `dry_penalty_last_n` default | 64; a negative value turns DRY off (libllama) or is rejected (llama-server) | -1, the whole context |
| negative `dry_multiplier` | accepted, and the penalty becomes a bonus | rejected |
| `dry_base` below 1.0 | llama-server uses its default | negative rejected, else DRY stays off, with a warning when `dry_multiplier` is set |
| empty breaker list | rejected by llama-server | accepted |
| breaker count | no cap | 64 |
| breaker length | 40 bytes | 40 code points |
| breaker split across tokens | matched as a token sequence | not matched |

</details>

### Limitations

- Speculative decoding is refused in `__init__`, since `validate_params` sees only `SamplingParams`. An engine with both fails to start.
- It needs the V2 model runner, the default. The V1 loader rejects it at startup.
- `LLM`'s `logits_processors` annotation (`vllm/entrypoints/llm.py:221`, line numbers at `68796a1530`) still names the V1 class, so mypy flags `LLM(logits_processors=[DryState])` although the runtime accepts it. No pre-commit hook type-checks `examples/`.
- Breakers resolve to token ids in `add_request`, inside `execute_model`. `__init__` decodes and indexes the vocabulary (0.7 to 2.7 s in engine init for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on the RTX 5050 box) and resolves the default set, so requests with the default breakers resolve nothing. A new set costs an index lookup per single-character breaker and a vocabulary scan per longer one.
- Each worker holds its own tokenizer, decoded vocabulary and character index in host memory. Under `skip_tokenizer_init`, DRY runs without breakers after one warning.
- `__init__` also runs `dry_core` once so that CUDA loads its kernels at startup, adding about 1.05 to 1.5 s on an RTX 5050 to each engine start that loads the processor (7.3 s once, with the load average above 50). Non-last PP ranks pay it too, as processors are built before the last-rank check.
- A `dry_base` at or below 1.000001 takes a sequential Python scan that copies the window to the host inside `gpu_sync_allowed()` and holds the GIL. So does an `allowed_length + max_exponent` above 2048, which at the default allowed length means a base below about 1.044.
- A DRY request whose context never repeats still pays a vocabulary-sized accumulator and an `index_add_` every step, since skipping them would need a device read. The default window is the whole context, so the match scan grows with it.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_dry.py
python examples/features/logits_processor/dry.py
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files examples/features/logits_processor/README.md \
    examples/features/logits_processor/dry.py tests/v1/sample/test_dry.py
```

An out-of-tree harness runs the sync and TP=2 checks below, loading DRY by FQCN.

## Test Result

DCO and Mergify ran. The rest of CI is waiting on a `ready` label.

Tests, the demo and the sync check ran at `68796a1530` on an RTX 5050. The TP=2 runs used two RTX PRO 6000s at `e25349dec6`.

- All 42 tests in `test_dry.py` passed, the four CUDA-only ones included. They check the port against llama.cpp's worked example and a brute-force oracle, and one runs `BatchSharder.shard_sampler_inputs` for 2 and 3 simulated ranks with its Triton plan kernel replaced.
- pre-commit passes at both of the PR's commits.
- A live Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct engine serving DRY requests exits 0 under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, eager and with CUDA graphs, and two further runs exit 0, one with no engine that shows the checker firing and one that times breaker resolution.
- At `tensor_parallel_size=2`, Qwen3.8-27B and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8 ran with and without `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`. Each rank sampled only its own rows, and the check caught nothing. Token ids matched except on two long DRY rows on Qwen with CUDA graphs (two of three runs), at a near-tie where DRY penalized nothing. On Qwen, DRY's penalties were bit-identical wherever the token histories agreed.
- The demo exits 0 and prints the two outputs quoted in the example's docstring. Without DRY, facebook/opt-125m repeats one sentence five times.
- Nothing here tests the HTTP serving path, per-step cost, output quality with DRY on, or a differential against the llama.cpp binary.

<details><summary>Environment and measurement notes</summary>

The runs at `68796a1530` used the upstream wheel matching `dd3bc9c72f`, with FlashInfer at the pinned 0.7.0. The TP=2 runs at `e25349dec6`, which has the same DRY code in its earlier in-tree layout on an older main (`f34a0e0797`), used an editable install over the compiled extensions of an older main's wheel, `410f6da5c4`, with FlashInfer 0.6.18. They also loaded a stand-in `libnvidia-ml.so.1` that hid the RTX 5050 from NVML's device enumeration and lookups and passed every other call to the real library. The 5050 runs did not.

The live-engine check runs Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with `max_model_len=512`. Each engine gets greedy 24-token requests with DRY on the default breakers, DRY on an unseen breaker set, a degenerate base, DRY off, and a batch of five. The DRY requests set `dry_multiplier=0.8`, `dry_base=1.75`, `dry_allowed_length=2` and `dry_penalty_last_n=64`. The CUDA-graph engine uses `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. The degenerate base, `dry_base=1.000001`, takes the Python fallback, and the check stays silent there because its host copy is declared. The in-process engine times the vocabulary pass at init (2012.3 ms) and counts 0 passes while serving. The check is off until engine setup ends, so a separate run without an engine constructs a `DryState` under it. That run also shows the checker raising on an undeclared `.item()` and on a non-blocking copy from pageable memory, and staying silent inside `gpu_sync_allowed()`.

The 2012.3 ms pass came from a run under heavy host load. The same pass measured 850.2 ms in an earlier run with a load of 1.3 and 674.0 ms in one that recorded none. One older run measured 2669.6 ms.

The warmup range comes from six processes at `68796a1530`, three eager and three with CUDA graphs. Five measured `_warm_up_dry_core` at 1054.9 to 1497.3 ms. A sixth measured 7335.5 ms with the host load average at 52.8 after it and is left out of the range.

Breaker resolution was timed on the CPU with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct's tokenizer at `ec74785c7a`, whose resolution code is the same. With the vocabulary already decoded, a new set of `.`, `,` and newline took 0.8 ms on first use on a quiet host, and `</s>`, `###` and a tab took 10.6 ms. Reruns under host load took 0.9 to 22.6 ms and 10.5 to 193 ms. A set already seen took 0.006 ms. At `4196581563` the character index holds 12.3 MiB next to the decoded texts' 9.0 MiB.

The TP=2 runs keep the engine core in-process and queue the same eight rows before the first step, DRY on and off, for 24 steps in both engines. `enable_batch_sharded_sampling` is a `ParallelConfig.compute_hash` factor, so the sharded engine compiles separately. Read-only probe processors on either side of DRY record each rank's rows and the penalties. Llama used CUTLASS FP8 and `TRITON_ATTN`, since FlashInfer's JIT here needs CUDA 12.9 for SM 12.x.

The demo ran under a `sitecustomize` hook that sets `gpu_memory_utilization` to 0.55 on the 5050, since the demo passes none, from a directory that links the tree's `examples/` and `tests/` next to the installed wheel.

</details>

Per `AGENTS.md` section 1: AI assistance was used for this change and for this description. Test commands and their results are the two sections above.

Enable Kimi-K3 DSpark support in MoRIIO hybrid READ without changing the wire format.

- Recognize wrapped full-attention groups shared by the target and drafter.

- Bound the decode-only attention tail using padded target rows and drafter lookahead, applying DCP scaling only to sharded attention specs.
- Share `clip_ssm_state_blocks` with NIXL while preserving its existing behavior.

The change is limited to MoRIIO block selection and the shared clipping helper. It adds no scheduler policy, model-runner, or GPU synchronization changes. DSpark requires Mamba `align` mode and a single transferable attention group; unsupported hybrid configurations remain rejected.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Mint the CRCR report's OIDC token after the wait, not before
commits.pr_body:
## The bug

Every CRCR nightly report is failing with a 401 on every job. From build
[91827](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91827):

```
[2026-09-29T17:07:33Z]   401 for :nvidia: (H200 MIG 18GB) Basic Models (Initialization): {"detail": "Invalid authorization token"}
...
[2026-09-29T17:07:56Z] reported 0 job(s), 360 failed
```

The relay is right to reject it: the token was expired.

`crcr-report.sh` mints the Buildkite OIDC token at the top of the script, then
enters the poll loop that waits for the rest of the build, and only uses the
token once that loop exits. `buildkite-agent oidc request-token` is called
without `--lifetime`, so the token's `exp` defaults to five minutes. In build
91827 the step ran for 6h48m before reporting, so all 360 callbacks were sent
with a token that had expired roughly six and a half hours earlier.

This is a consequence of #58626 and #59066, which introduced the wait so the
report could no longer snapshot a build before its jobs finished. The wait was
added; the mint stayed where it was.

It is invisible in CI: the reporter logs and returns non-zero, the shell swallows
it (`|| echo ... best-effort`), the script `exit 0`s, and the step is `soft_fail`.
The step renders green while reporting nothing, so HUD has simply been missing
vLLM nightly data.

## The fix

Mint the token immediately before invoking `crcr_report.py`, where it needs to
live for the few seconds the callbacks take rather than for the whole build.

The mint at the top is kept as a pre-flight check and its value discarded, so an
unusable OIDC setup still fails in seconds instead of being discovered after
hours of polling.

Raising `--lifetime` instead was considered and rejected: the wait is bounded by
the build-age deadline, not by any figure a lifetime could safely cover, and a
multi-hour cross-org bearer token defeats the point of using OIDC.

## Also here

`CRCR_MAX_BUILD_AGE_S` default drops from 25200s (7h) to 14400s (4h).

Flagging this one for review rather than asserting it is free. It is
independent of the token fix, and it cuts the other way: build 91827 hit the
7h deadline with jobs still running, and `crcr_report.py` drops non-terminal
jobs rather than reporting them, so a shorter deadline means a thinner nightly
in HUD. Happy to drop this hunk and land the token fix alone if reviewers would
rather set the deadline from a distribution of recent nightly durations.

## Test plan

`bash -n .buildkite/scripts/crcr-report.sh` passes. The path only executes in the
torch-nightly lane on `main`, so it is verified by the next nightly: the step
should log `reported <N> job(s), 0 failed` instead of `reported 0 job(s), 360 failed`,
and `hud.pytorch.org/crcr/vllm-project/vllm?event=nightly` should show the run.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Attach resolved logprobs to streaming derender chunks
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Complete the streaming-logprobs limitation deferred in RFC #47161's PR-1 ("logprobs are dropped on the streaming path as a known limitation"): the streaming derender endpoints accepted `GenerateResponseStreamChoice.logprobs` from the generate worker but never resolved or attached them — only non-streaming derender resolved the `token_id:N` placeholders. An OpenAI client streaming with `logprobs: true` through a token-in/token-out router received no logprobs. This PR attaches the existing resolution to the streaming paths; the broader `GenerateLogProbs` shape redesign is now defined in #57574 (implementation in #58181, sequenced after this PR).

The fix resolves placeholders per chunk on both streaming paths and attaches them to the output choices (both `ChatCompletionResponseStreamChoice` and `CompletionResponseStreamChoice` already had the fields). Two small, bounded additions to the client-carried `DerenderStreamState` keep resolution correct across chunk boundaries without breaking the stateless protocol:

- `logprob_context_token_ids` (max 4 entries — exactly the window `_correct_decoded_token` reads): seeds byte-fallback (U+FFFD) correction so multi-byte characters whose tokens split across chunks still resolve to real strings.
- `logprob_text_offset`: keeps completion-logprobs `text_offset` absolute across chunks, mirroring `initial_text_offset` in the generate streaming path (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py`).

Docs: `derenderer.md` gains a "Streaming state and logprobs" section covering the new fields and behavior (the limitation was previously undocumented there), and the stale bullet describing streaming derender as unsupported is refreshed.

**Not a duplicate:** searched open/closed PRs and issues for derender + logprobs / streaming logprobs; nothing addresses this. #50550 (parser-aware streaming derender, in review) does not touch logprobs — its parsed path constructs stream choices without them and will need the same treatment as a follow-up once it lands (a code comment now flags the parser-path logprobs/hidden-reasoning suppression for that work).

No model-output changes: this affects only frontend response-processing parity, so no model evals are applicable.

## Test Plan

New unit tests (real tokenizer on a tiny model, stub renderer — no server, matching the existing pattern in the file):

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -q
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -q
```

Covered behaviors: per-chunk placeholder resolution (chat), byte-fallback correction across chunk boundaries (one token per chunk of a byte-split emoji), absolute `text_offset` continuation (completions), state boundedness (context tail never exceeds 4), and a control test that chunks without logprobs keep `logprobs: null`.

Lint:

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py --hook-stage manual
```

## Test Result

- New tests: 5/5 pass with the change; **4/5 fail without it** (missing logprobs on streamed choices), with the no-logprobs control correctly passing on both.
- Full derender suites: **71 passed** (36 streaming + 35 endpoint tests).
- All pre-commit hooks passed, including CI-style `mypy-3.12` (manual stage).

## AI-assisted contribution

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). Every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, who ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DP] add_dp_placement_groups does not require ray[default]
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #23822.

That PR removed the `ray.util.state.list_nodes()` call from `CoreEngineActorManager.create_dp_placement_groups()` because `list_nodes()` is a developer API backed by the Ray dashboard HTTP server (`127.0.0.1:8265/api/v0/nodes`), which only exists when Ray is installed as `ray[default]` and started with the dashboard. vLLM does not depend on `ray[default]`.

The sibling `add_dp_placement_groups()` (used by `scale_up_elastic_ep()` for elastic EP scale-up) still called `list_nodes()`, so `/scale_elastic_ep` fails with `Failed to connect to API server` on any Ray cluster started without the dashboard, e.g. `ray` core only or `ray start --include-dashboard=False`. Downstream projects have had to monkeypatch `ray.util.state.list_nodes` around the call to work around this (NVIDIA Dynamo, `components/src/dynamo/vllm/handlers.py`, `TODO(upstream-vllm)` block in `scale_elastic_ep`).

This PR applies the same fix as #23822 to `add_dp_placement_groups()`:

- Drop the `ray.util.state.list_nodes` import.
- Use `available_resources_per_node()` (already imported there, keyed by node id, live nodes only) to enumerate nodes, and locate the DP master node via its `node:<dp_master_ip>` resource key, exactly as `create_dp_placement_groups()` does today.
- Read each node's IP with the existing `_node_ip_from_resources()` helper.

Placement group bundles, names (`dp_rank_{rank}`), strategy (`STRICT_PACK`), and the local DP rank computation are unchanged. The old "there can only be one head node" check is kept.

## Test Plan

New unit tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py`:

- Mock a Ray cluster with two GPU nodes and one CPU-only node, with the DP master deliberately not first.
- Replace `ray.util.state.list_nodes` with a function that raises, so any regression back to the dashboard API fails the tests.
- Cover: multi-node growth, TP>1 growth, no-growth early return, missing master node.

```shell
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py -q
```

End-to-end on one node with 4x RTX PRO 5000 (vLLM 0.29.0 wheel + this patch, ray 2.58.0), same model and flags as `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py`. Ray is started **without** the dashboard, i.e. the no-`ray[default]` case:

```shell
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0   # sm120: FlashInfer sampler rejects the arch
ray start --head --include-dashboard=False --num-gpus 4 --disable-usage-stats
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-backend ray \
  --enable-expert-parallel --enable-eplb --eplb-config.use_async=false --enable-elastic-ep \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --port 8006
curl -X POST localhost:8006/scale_elastic_ep -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"new_data_parallel_size": 4}'
```

## Test Result

With this change:

```
7 passed in 40.39s
```

Without the `utils.py` change (tests only), 3 of the 4 new tests fail with
`AssertionError: ray.util.state.list_nodes() must not be called ...`; the remaining one is the no-growth early return.

`pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/utils.py tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py`: ruff check / ruff format / typos / mypy all pass.

End-to-end, scale 2 -> 4 on the dashboard-less Ray cluster:

Before (0.29.0 as released):
```
ERROR [api_router.py:79] Scale failed: Failed to make request to http://127.0.0.1:8265/api/v0/nodes. Failed to connect to API server. Please check the API server log for details. Make sure dependencies are installed with `pip install ray[default]`.
POST /scale_elastic_ep -> 500 {"error":{"message":"Scale failed", ...}}
```

After (this patch):
```
POST /scale_elastic_ep -> 200 {"message":"Scaled to 4 data parallel engines"}   # 43 s
(Worker_DP2_EP2) [EP Rank 2/4] Expert parallelism is enabled ... Local/global number of experts: 32/128
(Worker_DP3_EP3) [EP Rank 3/4] Expert parallelism is enabled ... Local/global number of experts: 32/128
```
All four GPUs hold an engine afterwards (~40 GB each), completions still return `" Paris."`, and a subsequent scale 4 -> 2 also returns 200.
AI assistance was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests myself.

commits.pr_title: [Mypy] Fix mypy typing for Zamba2 models
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR depends only on the W-model typing PR [#58254](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58254). The Z branch is rebased onto W, and its diff against W changes two files. The PR base remains `main`, so GitHub also shows W's changes until W merges.

Continue the incremental mypy rollout tracked by [#26533](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26533) by removing `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[zZ]"` from the mypy exclusions. This adds `zamba2.py`, the only selected Z-model file, to type checking.

Zamba2's LoRA output projection is constructed within each dimension-type branch, so the merged projection receives `list[int]` and the ordinary projection receives `int`. The MLP's `num_hybrid_layers` annotation changes from `dict[int, int]` to `int`, matching its callers and use in `range`. Constructor arguments and model computations are unchanged. No casts or typing suppressions are added.

## Reproducer

On W at `f52cbfe437`, remove `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[zZ]"` from `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, then run:

```bash
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 \
  --files vllm/model_executor/models/zamba2.py \
  --hook-stage manual
```

Base (W `f52cbfe437`):


commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Skip engine-derived metrics under `--disable-log-stats`
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `--disable-log-stats`, the engine runs with `log_stats=False`: `Scheduler.make_stats()` returns `None` and request lifecycle events (`QUEUED` / `SCHEDULED` / `PREEMPTED`) are not recorded. The Python frontend exports no `vllm:*` engine or request metrics in this mode. The Rust frontend kept exporting metrics derived from that missing data, with misleading values:

- Scheduler gauges (`vllm:num_requests_running`, `vllm:num_requests_waiting`, `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc`, prefix cache, spec decode, ...) are created eagerly per engine and stay at `0` forever. Consumers such as autoscalers or an inference-gateway endpoint picker would see every replica as idle.
- `vllm:request_queue_time_seconds`, `vllm:request_prefill_time_seconds`, and `vllm:request_inference_time_seconds` observe `0` for every request, and the preemption counters stay at `0`.
- `vllm:lora_requests_info` never sees `SCHEDULED` events, so every in-flight adapter is reported as waiting.

This PR adds `EngineCoreClientConfig::engine_stats_enabled` (set from `!disable_log_stats` by the server) and skips those metrics when engines do not record stats:

- The scheduler-stats recorder and the LoRA info exporter are only created when engine stats are enabled. Routing still consumes scheduler stats whenever they arrive.
- The event-derived request metrics are grouped into `EventMetricHandles`, resolved only when engine stats are enabled.
- Metrics the frontend observes itself (TTFT, ITL, E2E latency, decode time, TPOT, token counters including cached prompt tokens, `request_success`) are still exported, since `prefill_stats` and output timestamps do not depend on `log_stats`.

The `--disable-log-stats` help text now also mentions the skipped metrics.

Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses `--disable-log-stats` metric behavior in the Rust frontend (searched open PRs for `disable-log-stats rust` and `log stats metrics Rust Frontend`).

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py --no-fail-fast
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

`generate_without_engine_stats_exports_only_frontend_observed_metrics` (`llm/tests/generate.rs`) drives a LoRA request through a mock engine that behaves like one started with `--disable-log-stats` (no events, no scheduler stats). It asserts that the adapter never appears in `/metrics` while the request is in flight, that frontend-observed metrics are exported, and that scheduler gauges and event-derived request metrics are absent. The existing metrics test additionally asserts `vllm:request_queue_time_seconds` on the stats-enabled path.

## Test Result

- Workspace nextest: 1891 passed, 13 skipped. `vllm-tool-parser-py` was excluded because its test binary cannot load `libpython3.14.so` in the local environment.
- clippy and fmt: clean.
- Reverting each gate separately (scheduler recorder, LoRA info, event-derived request metrics) makes the new test fail.
- Not yet validated end to end against a real engine with `--disable-log-stats`.

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Charge daemon-held weights against `gpu_memory_utilization`
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `--load-format ipc_cache` (zero-copy), the weights live in the daemon's allocations, so at engine startup they already count as "in use" and `request_memory`'s `free >= total * gpu_memory_utilization` check fails for any normal utilization. Users had to lower utilization to whatever the daemon left free.

This PR charges the memory already in use at startup against the budget as the weights' share, and returns the remainder as the engine's own allowance. The downstream KV cache computation is unchanged. If the memory in use already exceeds the budget, fail with a message pointing to *increase* utilization. The daemon also releases load-time transients (`gc.collect()` + `empty_cache()`) so they are not charged to the engine.

Assumption (in the docstring): everything in use on the device at startup belongs to the daemon.
